source_text: Χειροτονήσατε οὖν ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισκόπους καὶ διακόνους ἀξίους τοῦ κυρίου, ἄνδρας πραεῖς καὶ ἀφιλαργύρους καὶ ἀληθεῖς καὶ δεδοκιμασμένους: ὑμῖν γὰρ λειτουργοῦσι καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν λειτουργίαν τῶν προφητῶν καὶ διδασκάλων. μὴ οὖν ὑπερίδητε αὐτούς: αὐτοὶ γάρ εἰσιν οἱ τετιμημένοι ὑμῶν μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ διδασκάλων. Ἐλέγχετε δὲ ἀλλήλους μὴ ἐν ὀργῇ, ἀλλ’ ἐν εἰρήνῃ ὡς ἔχετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ: καὶ παντὶ ἀστοχοῦντι κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου μηδεὶς λαλείτω μηδὲ παῤ ὑμῶν ἀκουέτω, ἕως οὗ μετανοήσῃ. τὰς δὲ εὐχὰς ὑμῶν καὶ τὰς ἐλεημοσύνας καὶ πάσας τὰς πράξεις οὕτω ποιήσατε, ὡς ἔχετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
pass_a_gloss: So appoint for yourselves bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord, men gentle and not lovers of money and truthful and tested: for they serve you and themselves the service of the prophets and teachers. Do not therefore look down on them: for they are the ones honored among you with the prophets and teachers. But correct one another not in anger, but in peace as you have in the gospel: and to anyone missing the mark against the other let no one speak nor let him be heard among you, until he repents. The prayers of you and the acts of mercy and all the deeds do thus, as you have in the gospel of our Lord.

pass_b_english: To truly serve God, choose bishops and deacons who are worthy of the Lord - gentle, not driven by money, truthful, and proven in their faith. These leaders will serve both you and themselves as they carry out the work of the prophets and teachers, so give them the respect they deserve. In fact, they are honored among you, just like the prophets and teachers. When correcting each other, do it peacefully, as the gospel teaches, and not in anger. If someone has wronged another, don't engage with them or listen to their side of the story until they have repented. And when it comes to your prayers, acts of mercy, and all your actions, make sure to do them in the spirit of the gospel of our Lord.

review.notes: Pass B fails to maintain fidelity to the Greek and Pass A regarding the disciplinary instruction. The Greek 'καὶ παντὶ ἀστοχοῦντι κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου μηδεὶς λαλείτω μηδὲ παῤ ὑμῶν ἀκουέτω, ἕως οὗ μετανοήσῃ' (and to anyone missing the mark against the other let no one speak nor let him be heard among you, until he repents) is rendered in Pass B as 'If someone has wronged another, don't engage with them or listen to their side of the story until they have repented.' This changes the meaning from a prohibition on speaking to/hearing a person who has erred (a disciplinary exclusion) to a refusal to hear 'their side of the story' (a refusal of due process/defense), which contradicts the source's intent.
reasons: Pass B misinterprets the disciplinary clause 'μηδεὶς λαλείτω μηδὲ παῤ ὑμῶν ἀκουέτω' (let no one speak nor let him be heard among you) by translating it as 'don't engage with them or listen to their side of the story', which alters the agency and the nature of the prohibition.
